reminder.notes:
# Reminder 2.28.0

### Features

- Redesigned 3D glowing bell app icon with unified theme-adaptive squircle background and safe-zone alignment across Android devices and the app store website.
- Advanced reminder pausing: pause any reminder for hours, days, custom times, or indefinitely with seamless cloud sync (Drift schema v9), single-tap resume pill badges, and multi-select bulk pause.
- Full-screen alerts in all cases: eliminated heads-up banner degradation by enforcing Android 14+ background activity launch privileges (MODE_BACKGROUND_ACTIVITY_START_ALLOWED) and keyguard dismissal.
- Overhauled Upcoming screen for long lists: instant in-screen search bar, single streamlined filter row with category bottom sheet selector, and collapsible chronological section groups with item counts and expand/collapse all controls.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed Android 14+ background activity launch restrictions causing full-screen alarm screens to silently degrade to heads-up notification banners.
- Excluded paused reminders from overdue upcoming counts and filters.

mirrordrive.notes:
MirrorDrive 0.15.1 - Diagnostics finally have somewhere to go

The app has recorded technical failures for a long time and has never once been
able to send them. They were posted to a Tailscale hostname, on a tailnet no
phone was ever a member of, with no server behind it. Every incident queued on
the device to its hundred-item cap and was then dropped.

Nothing about the reporting changed here, because nothing about it was wrong.
It now has an address that exists.

### Features

- Diagnostics are sent to diagnostics.pnsjy.in, a real relay reached through
  the same tunnel as everything else. Consent and content are unchanged:
  allow-listed technical failures only, never file contents, paths or account
  state.

### Bug fixes

- The relay address pointed at a tailnet host that resolves nowhere. Every
  incident this app has ever recorded was queued and discarded.
- Removed two unused constants naming a Google Sheet that incidents do not go
  to. Nothing read them, and anyone reading the file would reasonably have
  believed otherwise.

### Notes

DIAGNOSTICS_RELAY still overrides the address at build time, so a debug build
can point at a local instance.

twinclean.notes:
TwinClean 1.3.3 - Buildable again

TwinClean could not be built at all. Two separate problems, neither in this
app's own code, and the app itself is unchanged by this release.

### Features

- Koi naya feature nahi. Ye release sirf isliye hai taaki app dobara ban sake.

### Bug fixes

- None in the app. Scanning, the duplicate rules and the UI are untouched.

### Notes

First, build_runner crashed inside the analyzer before producing a single file.
The Flutter SDK's own services/platform_views.dart now uses dot-shorthand
syntax and the pinned analyzer 7.6.0 has no visitor for it, so summarising
package:flutter/services.dart threw. Upgrading drift, drift_dev, drift_flutter
and build_runner brings an analyzer that parses the current SDK.
flutter_riverpod deliberately stays on 2.6.1 - letting the resolver choose
freely pulls Riverpod 3, which removed StateProvider and ChangeNotifierProvider
and produced 60 errors here.

Second, the release build failed compiling a file nobody wrote: the generated
plugin registrant could not find WorkmanagerPlugin. The cause was a federated
package resolving differently here than in the rest of the fleet - the same
constraint, resolved on a different day, gave workmanager_android 0.9.3 where
the Store and MirrorDrive both have 0.9.0+2. The class exists in both versions
under the same namespace, which is exactly why the error is so unhelpful. The
whole workmanager set is now pinned together to the versions the other apps
build with; pinning only the Android half is worse than pinning none, because
it pairs an old implementation with a newer interface.

A test that split file paths on '/' was also fixed. On Windows that returns the
whole path, so every basename comparison failed and the suite could never go
green on the machine this app is built on.

taashclub.notes:
Taash Club 1.19.3 - Resilient in-app updater and dynamic computer player AI

### Features
- Resilient In-App Updater: Auto-resumes interrupted downloads on app lifecycle resume, increases download retry budget to 8 attempts with exponential backoff, and performs APK integrity checks before attempting installation.
- Preserved Update Dialog: Retains download completion state across screen sleep and lockscreens so users can tap Install Now immediately upon unlocking.
- Dynamic Computer Bot AI: Integrated randomized decision-making and human-like gameplay variety across Gochi, Teen Do Paanch, and Kali Begum offline matches.
- Tactical AI Play Variety: Computer players now employ personality weighting, tactical suit-voiding passes, varied lead cards, and non-deterministic trump/sluff selections rather than rigid predictable moves.

### Bug fixes
- Fixed in-app updater failing when phone is locked or network sockets are suspended during background download.
- Fixed corrupt or truncated APK files triggering infinite retry loops by verifying file size and clearing damaged downloads.
- Fixed computer bots playing predictable, deterministic cards and bids in offline card matches.

cards.notes:
Cards 2.5.3 - Update checks move to the app store hub

### Features

- Update check ab app store hub se aata hai, wahi jagah jahan se baaki saari
  apps aati hain. Aapko farak nahi dikhega.

### Bug fixes

- The update check pointed at this app's own public mirror, which existed only
  to be readable without a token. It is no longer needed.

### Notes

Every app publishes its APK to app-store-web under a fixed tag, and the store
already reads from there. Polling a per-app public repo as well meant each app
needed a public repository of its own purely to be readable - and one of those,
for another app, turned out to be a full public source mirror. One public
repository for the whole fleet is fewer places for that to happen.

Nothing about this app changed. Same scanning, same vault, same encryption, and
still no network code beyond the update check.

langkeeper.notes:
# LangKeeper 0.1.0-beta.4 - Google Sign-In Credential Manager Alignment

### Features

- Credential Manager Flow Optimization: Removed scopeHint from initial authenticate() calls to ensure clean identity authentication across Android devices running Google Play Services Credential Manager.
- Incremental Authorization Model: Hidden Google Drive appDataFolder authorization is cleanly requested on-demand when cloud backup or restore actions execute.

### Bug fixes

- Fixed Android Credential Manager reauthentication failure ([16] Account reauth failed) triggered when scopeHint conflicted with initial user sign-in.
- Maintained detailed error handling and one-tap signing certificate copy in AuthTroubleshootDialog for clear diagnostic feedback.
